text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan to be questioned by parliament on Tuesday over alleged irregularities in key economic bodies. He is the first minister to be questioned by parliament since last October's elections.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah receives Kuwaiti students in Britain. Sheikh Saad flew to Britain in March following an emergency colon operation at a Kuwaiti hospital.
- Richard Butler, the new executive chairman of the United Nations commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, will make his first visit to Kuwait on Friday.

- Government panel backs Sea Skua missiles. No deal yet signed with British Aerospace. Parliament's protection of public funds committee met on Monday to review the deal which experts said could be worth up to $150 million.
- Health Ministry official says 40 percent of Kuwait residents favour private sector medical services but they turn to public sector hospitals in the welfare state in case of complicated operations.
- It is in the interest of the military to finalise the missile deal, acting prime minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al- Sabah tells parliament's protection of public funds committee.
